essence: Consecration confers teaching authority, not fitness: the initiated son becomes a teacher only by abhiṣeka.
The guru must know the joining of the paths; Kāmika and Siddhayogīśvarīmata are cited to bind the Trika guru to the widest Śaiva standard.
The rite is sixty-four sprinklings, then one with mantra-charged water, and the instruments pass to the disciple.
A lineage is a lamp from a lamp: transmission frees the giver and must not be broken before death.
Authority is a duty-set — protection of the seven sacrifices and a hand lent to the falling.

rasa.justification: The chapter moves from exam to duty to rite to succession; the tone is custodial, not ecstatic — the steadiness of a lineage being handed on.
